column3: The SELECT statement is used to query the database. (sqlite.org/lang_select.html)
The result of a SELECT is zero or more rows of data where each row has a fixed number of columns. (sqlite.org/lang_select.html)
FROM clause processing: The input data for the simple SELECT is determined. (sqlite.org/lang_select.html)
The input data is either implicitly a single row with 0 columns (if there is no FROM clause) or is determined by the FROM clause. (sqlite.org/lang_select.html)
WHERE clause processing: The input data is filtered using the WHERE clause expression. (sqlite.org/lang_select.html)
If a WHERE clause is specified, the WHERE expression is evaluated for each row in the input data as a boolean expression. (sqlite.org/lang_select.html)

If the SELECT statement is an aggregate query with a GROUP BY clause, then each of the expressions specified as part of the GROUP BY clause is evaluated for each row of the dataset according to the processing rules stated below for ORDER BY expressions. (sqlite.org/lang_select.html)
As the components of a compound SELECT must be simple SELECT statements, they may not contain ORDER BY or LIMIT clauses. (sqlite.org/lang_select.html)

GROUP BY, HAVING and result-column expression processing: The set of result rows is computed by aggregating the data according to any GROUP BY clause and calculating the result-set expressions for the rows of the filtered input dataset. (sqlite.org/lang_select.html)
A simple SELECT statement is an aggregate query if it contains either a GROUP BY clause or one or more aggregate functions in the result-set. (sqlite.org/lang_select.html)
Each ORDER BY expression may be optionally followed by one of the keywords ASC (smaller values are returned first) or DESC (larger values are returned first). (sqlite.org/lang_select.html)
If neither ASC or DESC are specified, rows are sorted in ascending (smaller values first) order by default. (sqlite.org/lang_select.html)
As the components of a compound SELECT must be simple SELECT statements, they may not contain ORDER BY or LIMIT clauses. (sqlite.org/lang_select.html)
ORDER BY and LIMIT clauses may only occur at the end of the entire compound SELECT, and then only if the final element of the compound is not a VALUES clause. (sqlite.org/lang_select.html)

The INSERT statement comes in three basic forms. (sqlite.org/lang_insert.html)
The second form of the INSERT statement contains a SELECT statement instead of a VALUES clause. (sqlite.org/lang_insert.html)
The first form (with the "VALUES" keyword) creates one or more new rows in an existing table. (sqlite.org/lang_insert.html)

In this case the result of evaluating the left-most expression from each term of the VALUES list is inserted into the left-most column of each new row, and so forth for each subsequent expression. (sqlite.org/lang_insert.html)

An UPDATE statement is used to modify a subset of the values stored in zero or more rows of the database table identified by the qualified-table-name specified as part of the UPDATE statement. (sqlite.org/lang_update.html)
If the UPDATE statement does not have a WHERE clause, all rows in the table are modified by the UPDATE. (sqlite.org/lang_update.html)
The modifications made to each row affected by an UPDATE statement are determined by the list of assignments following the SET keyword. (sqlite.org/lang_update.html)

Beginning in SQLite version 3.15.0 (2016-10-14), an assignment in the SET clause can be a parenthesized list of column names on the left and a row value of the same size on the right. (sqlite.org/lang_update.html)

The instr(X,Y) function finds the first occurrence of string Y within string X and returns the number of prior characters plus 1, or 0 if Y is nowhere found within X. (sqlite.org/lang_corefunc.html)

Or, if X and Y are both BLOBs, then instr(X,Y) returns one more than the number of bytes prior to the first occurrence of Y, or 0 if Y does not occur anywhere within X. (sqlite.org/lang_corefunc.html)
The substr(X,Y,Z) function returns a substring of input string X that begins with the Y-th character and which is Z characters long. (sqlite.org/lang_corefunc.html)
If Z is omitted then substr(X,Y) returns all characters through the end of the string X beginning with the Y-th. (sqlite.org/lang_corefunc.html)
